scripted_findings.title: Brand identity is not anchored to any external profile
scripted_findings.evidence: None of the 2 crawled page(s) declares Organization, LocalBusiness or similar structured data with sameAs links. Without sameAs, an assistant has nothing distinguishing this brand from others sharing the name, which is the standard cause of mistaken identity.

scripted_findings.title: No viewport meta tag on 2 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: 2/2 crawled page(s) have no <meta name="viewport"> at all. Examples: ['https://www.paulgraham.com/', 'https://www.paulgraham.com/prepare.html']. Without it, mobile browsers lay the page out at a desktop width (about 980px) and shrink it to fit, so text is unreadable until the visitor pinch-zooms.

scripted_findings.title: Images missing alt attributes on 1 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: https://www.paulgraham.com/: 3/3 images have no alt attribute. Tracking pixels, images inside <noscript> and images marked presentational or aria-hidden are not counted.

scripted_findings.title: No usable XML sitemap discovered
scripted_findings.evidence: robots.txt declared 1 sitemap(s) and /sitemap.xml yielded no parsable <loc> entries. Crawlers then rely entirely on link discovery.

scripted_findings.title: No lang attribute on 2 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: 2/2 pages omit <html lang>. Examples: ['https://www.paulgraham.com/', 'https://www.paulgraham.com/prepare.html']. Language declaration affects pronunciation in screen readers and helps any consumer pick the right processing rules.

scripted_findings.title: No h1 heading on 2 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: 2/2 pages contain no h1 element at all. Examples: ['https://www.paulgraham.com/', 'https://www.paulgraham.com/prepare.html']. Extractors and assistants use the top heading to decide what a page is about.

scripted_findings.title: No structured data on 1 significant page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: 1/2 crawled pages of type ['home'] contain no JSON-LD. Structured data is read by the indexing crawlers that build the search index assistants query, and it states a fact with a type attached. Examples: ['https://www.paulgraham.com/']

pages.title: How Universities Should Prepare Founders
pages.text_excerpt: How Universities Should Prepare Founders August 2026 How should universities prepare students to start startups? Y Combinator is in the perfect position to answer this question, because we get them next. We're like grad school. And because YC has had 20 years to refine its model of what a promising founder looks like, you probably won't find a better target. What do the YC partners look for? It's surprisingly simple. They want people who are good at building things and have a habit of doing it. The hard part of startups is product: knowing what to build, and being able to build it.
